title: Privilege-change stream normalizer and tiered retention sampler for RBACv2 and SSO events
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: RBAC v2 introduced richer, high-volume authorization events (role grants/revokes, policy changes), and our SSO/SAML pipeline emits a higher cardinality of identity enrichment events. Combined these increases cause large ingestion bursts and index bloat. We need a production-safe pipeline component that: 1) normalizes privilege-change and SSO events into a canonical shape across versions, 2) applies sensitivity-based sampling and tiering at ingest (hot -> warm -> cold), 3) partitions and indexes to bound query cost, and 4) enforces per-tenant cost/retention SLAs with backpressure and compensating rehydration paths for compliance/legal requests.
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalizer emits a stable schema for privilege-change and SAML/SSO events with version tag and mapping rules; existing consumers (console, alerting, compliance search) can read canonical events with no schema errors
Ingest sampler reduces low-sensitivity event volume by >= 60% for top 10% tenants without dropping high-sensitivity events (sensitivity scoring must be deterministic and testable)
Tiered retention policy implemented: hot (7d full index), warm (30d compacted index), cold (90d archival blobs) with automated rollover and verification jobs
Partitioning scheme created (org_id/date/hour) that bounds daily shard growth and reduces cross-tenant fanout for queries
Cost guardrail enforcer rejects or routes excess tenant traffic to sampling with clear logs and tenant-facing metric emitted
Migration plan and scripts to reprocess last 90 days of RBAC events into canonical format with a validation job that compares event counts and hashes
Operability: dashboards for ingestion rate, sampling rate by tenant, partition distribution, coldstore retrieval latencies, and alert thresholds documented
Security review completed and KMS/HSM encryption validated for coldstore keys
design_notes: Normalization: map historical RBAC v1 fields into v2 canonical keys (actor.id, actor.type, target.resource, action, policy_id) and add event_version and sensitivity_score meta fields

Sensitivity scoring: deterministic ruleset (role_admin=true => high; policy_change=true => high; token_issued=false + read_only=true => low). Score range 0-100; threshold configurable per-tenant. Use feature flags for gradual rollout.

Sampling model: reservoir sampler per (org_id, event_type) with deterministic hashing on event_id to ensure reproducible sample set for audits. Low-sensitivity events are sampled aggressively; high-sensitivity never sampled.

Partitioning: primary partition by org_id and day (YYYY-MM-DD). Within-day secondary buckets by hour for write parallelism. Avoid tenant-hotspot by mapping large tenants to dedicated hot shards via tenant->shard mapping table.
Indexing: index only three fields for warm/cold tiers: event_ts, event_type, principal_id. Full JSON stored as compressed blob in warm/cold; hot tier has parsed fields for fast queries.
Coldstore: use configurable object prefix and compacted delta snapshots every 24h. Support fast rehydrate API that pulls and replays to warm store for e-discovery within SLA.
Cost controls: per-tenant daily budget counter; when budget exceeded, system switches tenant to sampling mode + rate limit. Telemetry emitted to billing and tenant console.
Backpressure: ingest gateway returns 429 with structured hint (retry-after, fallback sampling rate) when global or tenant-level budget thresholds crossed. Implement client SDK guidance UI in Console.

Migration approach: streaming rewriter that consumes historical raw audit topic, normalizes, writes to new topic plus verification stream (hash compare). Run in canaries for three large tenants before org-wide roll.

Trade-offs: heavier compute at ingest vs lower long-term storage cost. We accept extra CPU in ingest path to avoid quadratic query costs in cold store. Deterministic sampling chosen over probabilistic to satisfy compliance traceability.
